prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I get a rosé that is a little sweet and nice and crisp, but something unusual I have never heard of?"

List A:
Wine 1: Rosé, France, $20. Tasting note: "Crisp and fruity, this is a classic rosé. It shows a lightness that comes from the delicately handled fruits, giving gentle berry flavors, bright acidity and a textured aftertaste."
Wine 2: Rosé, Portugal, $12. Tasting note: "A sweet rosé that is light and fresh from the crisp raspberry acidity. It is bright and fruity, ready to drink."
Wine 3: Syrah, US, $20. Tasting note: "A pretty good rosé, full-bodied and robust in black cherry, strawberry, Dr. Pepper cola, rosehip tea and spice flavors. It finishes a little sweet."
Wine 4: Mourvèdre, US, $18. Tasting note: "A lovely rosé, dry and crisp, with peach skin, orange, strawberry and white pepper flavors, highlighted by brisk acidity. Would score higher if not for a certain heaviness."
Wine 5: Rosé, US, $16. Tasting note: "A good rosé, crisp and light-bodied. It has rich strawberry, orange zest, vanilla and spice flavors. Nice and silky in the mouth, as a blush wine should be, but it's a little on the sweet side."

List B:
Wine 1: Rosé, France, $20. Tasting note: "This crisp, dry rosé is very fresh with delicious acidity. It has a bright character, lively and full of raspberry flavors. Drink now."
Wine 2: Pinot Noir, US, $18. Tasting note: "A good rosé, fruity and spicy and crisp in acids. It's a bit on the sweet side, but otherwise offers pleasant flavors of strawberries, raspberries, herb tea and spices."
Wine 3: Rosé, Italy, $8. Tasting note: "This brightly colored rosé from northeastern Italy offers aromas of small berry fruit and delicate floral tones. It tastes clean and crisp and leaves a cheerful endnote of fresh berry flavors."
Wine 4: Rosé, US, $16. Tasting note: "This excellent rosé is one of a handful given extra bottle age before release, and it rewards that time with unusual flavors––rhubarb and strawberry, hints of banana and a touch of creamsicle in the fade. Not typical in any way, but tasty and full-bodied."
Wine 5: Sparkling Blend, South Africa, $30. Tasting note: "This delicious rosé is a combination of sweet strawberry and a touch of lemon crispness on the nose and the palate. Its light, elegant character is supported by a dancing acidity and a balance of ripe berry flavors and minerality. A great food pairing choice or stellar solo sip."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
